clue.text: Dashing manner of personal assistant can upset ambassador

indicators.note: upset means the three letters of the word can are knocked into a new order

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the formal title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A secretary's tin is knocked over by a visiting diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' reads as a verb in the surface, but it is the noun being knocked over by 'upset'; an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence and style, a dashing way of carrying oneself.

clue.text: Fire cleric for wearing it?

parts.note: to fire someone is to give them the sack
the cloth is a term for the clergy, as in a man of the cloth

explanation.surface: A disgraced clergyman is dismissed and dressed in penitential garb.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a sacked cleric might well wear sackcloth as a sign of penitence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sackcloth is coarse fabric traditionally worn as a show of mourning or repentance, fitting for a defrocked priest.

clue.text: Escorting lady with carriage to play card game

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: to play suggests the letters of the game's name are moved about freely

parts.note: loo is an old card game

explanation.surface: A woman out with a chaperone takes a coach to a card party.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo was a popular gambling card game in earlier centuries; 'to play' shuffles its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to accompany a woman socially, a hired escort.

clue.text: One way to damage the ultimate?

definitions.text: One way to damage the ultimate?

indicators.note: damage here means the letters of the word ultimate are mangled into another order

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about how one might spoil the very best thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is definition and wordplay at once: jumbling ULTIMATE is literally a way of mangling it.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutilate something is to damage it severely by disfiguring it.

clue.text: Cash on delivery?

parts.note: the familiar commercial phrase is reread as money paid out when a mother is delivered of a baby

explanation.definitionFit: These were state payments to mothers around childbirth, money given on the delivery of a baby.

clue.text: Drawing for the pamphlet I take on

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: An artist sketches for the leaflet he has agreed to produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is the action of drawing or pulling a load over a surface.

clue.text: Left port with cargo

parts.note: Aden is a port city in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship sailed out of harbour fully loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or carrying a heavy burden, as a ship full of freight.

clue.text: Beat heavily though latterly a light-weight

definitions.text: Beat heavily though latterly a light-weight

parts.words: Beat heavily though latterly a light-weight
parts.note: a word meaning to thrash soundly whose final five letters spell a small unit of weight

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the contradiction: a word for a heavy beating ends in OUNCE, one of the lightest weights.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce an opponent is to defeat or thrash them decisively.

clue.text: Is a far-out excursion

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the words is a far are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A trip that goes to remote places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far-out' looks like one adjective, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on IS A FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition or trip, especially to observe wild animals in Africa.

clue.text: Contributing factor to drop in performance?

definitions.text: Contributing factor to drop in performance?

parts.words: Contributing factor to drop in performance?
parts.note: a phrase sounding like a cause of decline is read literally as a device that lets an actor fall through the stage during a show

explanation.definitionFit: A stage has a hinged opening in its floor through which performers can descend or vanish mid-show.

clue.text: Pluck feathers? Something much stiffer!

parts.note: pluck suggests courage, and feathers are contrasted with a far more rigid structure of the body

explanation.walkthrough: Pluck means courage, and the spine is a much stiffer support than a quill.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbone means firmness of character or courage, and literally the spine.

clue.text: Temporary accommodation in which' there is one occupant

indicators.note: in which tells us the second piece sits inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is shelter put up for a short stay
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A camping shelter housing a single camper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is someone who occupies a property, usually renting it.

clue.text: Fabric before long must be stretched over the room

indicators.note: stretched over says the first piece is pulled around the outside of the second

parts.note: soon means before long
a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: Cloth will soon need to be spread over the floor of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must' tempts the solver to start with the word for future obligation, but it belongs to the container phrase 'must be stretched over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shalloon is a light twilled woollen cloth used mainly for linings.

clue.text: Is awed by the figure — representing oil-trade

indicators.note: representing suggests the letters of oil-trade are made to stand in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is overawed by a statue that symbolises the petroleum business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is a link word; the definition describes a person who reveres an image.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, someone in thrall to a statue or graven image.

clue.text: Suma-wrestling with me, ten thrown! But it's just for fun

indicators.note: wrestling throws the letters of these words around into a new order

explanation.surface: Sumo wrestlers flinging ten opponents about is only a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suma' is a deliberate twist on sumo to supply the A; 'thrown' is a second hint that the letters are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement is entertainment or enjoyment, things done for fun.

clue.text: Cheeky first year student?

parts.note: cheeky suggests an impudent person, and that sense is joined to the word for a newcomer at university

explanation.walkthrough: Fresh can mean cheeky, so a cheeky man would be a fresh man.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshman is a student in their first year at college or university.

clue.text: The zip's gone!

parts.note: zip is slang for energy and vigour, so its loss describes a sluggish state rather than a broken fastener

explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is a lack of energy or enthusiasm, listless weariness.

clue.text: Having made the attempt, yesterday's try-out abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests the remaining letters are let loose into a new order

parts.note: the word is used in full here, the S included

explanation.surface: A test run from the day before was given up after a go at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' says TRY is taken from YESTERDAYS; 'abandoned' then shuffles the leftover YESEDAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Essayed is the past tense of essay, meaning to attempt or try.

clue.text: Quietly tell the priest

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to relate a story is to tell it

explanation.surface: Someone whispers a confession to the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a senior churchman such as a bishop, a high-ranking priest.

clue.text: Listing technical terms for it, boy admits failure

indicators.note: admits means the boy's name lets the other word inside it

parts.note: Gary is a boy's name
a loss is a failure or defeat

explanation.surface: A lad confesses he could not produce a jargon list.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is an alphabetical list of specialist words with their meanings.

clue.text: Bosses' improper haunt

indicators.note: improper suggests the letters are set in an incorrect arrangement

explanation.surface: Managers lurk around inappropriately.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess is to preoccupy the mind continually, as a thought that haunts someone.

clue.text: Perceives first engineer takes some food aboard ship

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for engineer or engineering

indicators.note: aboard places the food inside the letters for a ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual abbreviation for a ship
a pie is a dish of food

explanation.surface: A ship's chief engineer notices supplies being loaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts E at the front; 'takes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Espies means catches sight of or notices, so perceives.

clue.text: Religion I criticize

parts.note: to slam is to criticize harshly

explanation.surface: A believer finds fault with their faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith revealed through the Prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: Late-starter appears in rearranged embassy meeting

indicators.note: appears in says the letter goes inside the jumbled word
rearranged indicates the letters of embassy are set out in a fresh order
starter of late means just its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A latecomer turns up at a reorganised meeting at the embassy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' turns EMBASSY into ASSEMBY, and 'appears in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly is a gathering of people, a meeting.

clue.text: Man with cycle goes round the plant

indicators.note: goes round suggests the letters of man and cycle are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A man on a bicycle rides around a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclamen is a flowering plant with upswept petals, popular in pots.

clue.text: Legislative body seen at work

indicators.note: work, as in work into shape, signals the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lawmakers are observed busy on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is the upper chamber of a parliament or a governing council.

clue.text: Strange chaps set off out East to get left-overs

parts.note: odd means strange
men is a plural for chaps

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of set are jumbled once the compass letter is removed

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East, which goes out of the jumble

explanation.surface: Weird men head out east to collect scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram and 'out' the loss: SET without E leaves letters arranged as TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are odds and ends, bits remaining from a larger lot.
